common.agents:
Dynamics of change
expressed in silicon and priced in convexity.
common.silicon: confidential at rest, in transit, and in use — computed whole, on public silicon. degrees of freedom you exercise, leverage you widen, dependencies that never take hold. locally complete, networked across trillions of entrances and exits, each identity shifting, severed, and ephemeral.
common.thesis:
Distribution is not automatically decentralization. Distributing work across machines you don't own and can't see into only relocates the center. Each operator holds, in the clear, whatever their machine runs, so control, visibility, and leverage collect wherever the work lands — in the operators, the nodes, and in the chip vendor when attestation sits in the path. This is centralized distribution: the same concentration of power, call it neo-feudal, neo-monarchist, just spread across more locations. A whack-a-mole of centers. More masters. More overseers. Most systems that call themselves decentralized are built this way.

Decentralization is degrees of freedom held at once, at least two, usually many more.

Free alone — you can run and rebuild all of it yourself, and no one can lock you out. This is what the building blocks give: open software, open hardware, maps and kits to rebuild, matroidic privacy. Sovereignty.

Free when connected — you can join the network, exposure and dependencies don't build, and the exits and entrances are plentiful, minute, and never locked.

A rebuildable, transparent stack spans the first freedom. It spans nothing of the second. To do anything now, you connect — no man is an island — and connection seems to never be neutral: the moment what you're doing runs on someone else's machine, openness does nothing to keep that operator and intermediates from taking it in the clear. The other side builds dependencies.

Confidential computing spans the second freedom. It is what lets you connect with nothing to violate: a machine can run what you're doing, and there is nothing to take. Not hidden, simply never there in a form anyone could use. Nothing along the full path gains leverage. No dependency forms. The machine is a confidential node — distribution that builds no new center.

Emphasizing the descent to the silicon, you then have the option to be your own fab: a chip fab, a hardware fab, a software fab. It is a capacity that sits at every layer, exercised or not — a part that is open and fabricable builds no leverage. Make it, change it, or replace it. Nothing in the stack can lock you, nothing in it is closed to you. The deepest degree of freedom, fabrication all the way down.

economy.canonical: Each project maintains a principle canonical copy: the parts, the software, and the maps to build and fabricate, read, download, fork, remix, etch, flash. Forks branch off and multiply; testing on edge hardware refines the branched histories, run after run — proven in the metal, reversible either way.
economy.intro: The branches make a forest. Two roles work it: the treeliner at the edge, the cyberswagman traverses within.
economy.treeliner: The treeliner walks that frayed seam where the forest gives way to light, where day comes through in broken bars between the trunks and the dark thickens behind. The deep timber ahead, the daylight behind, the margin walked and walked again. Here the treeliner studies before the crossing: sizing the terrain, sharpening skill, reading where the going turns hard, a maker in the making, set to cross as the tools advance, miniaturize and run stitched into your pocket. Stake $MONA on a project and stay with it, iteration after iteration, diamond-handing it on the bet it comes good. A project that catches on gathers a crowd, and the crowd throws off prefab kit sales, wearable content, W3F merch, NFTs, Ganda minigames, Ionic appraisals, and level-ups around it. That activity fills a pool, and the treeliner who bet early and deep draws from it. Stake, spectate, walk the edge.
economy.cyberswagman: The cyberswagman traverses the forest, where the hunted just might become hunter. They may arrive green, prey to the beasts — the configurations that resist, the constraints that bite — and turn, pass after pass, into what runs them down. Deploy an agent, guided from a base template, trained on combinations of canonicals, set to run performance tests on edge hardware. The fight is the test: run after run on the metal, the cyberswagman takes the beasts and learns them, publishing another canonical from each pass, becoming stronger, ranging deeper, from first configurations — a quantized runtime that fits the accelerator, a sub-1B model that holds on the device, a pipeline that clears real-time latency — to a full open-source chip-fab project. The configurations that prove out accrue to the cyberswagman's stake from the project pool.

phases.title: offline signer
phases.hardware: SE051 Plug&Trust Click (NXP SE051C2 secure element) · Adafruit ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT Feather (240×135 IPS TFT + 3 buttons) · USB-C
phases.software: Rust no_std firmware (ESP32-S3, esp-hal) · secp256k1 · BIP-39/32/44 · NXP Plug & Trust (SE05x, I²C) · ST7789 display and button UI · USB-serial CLI
phases.desc: generates and holds keys on the secure element and signs on the device; multi-chain over secp256k1 (Bitcoin and EVM).

phases.title: local transcriber
phases.hardware: Raspberry Pi 5 or mini-PC · USB or I²S microphone · NVMe/microSD · optional NPU accelerator (Coral/Hailo)
phases.software: whisper.cpp or faster-whisper (small) · ggml or ONNX runtime · audio capture (PortAudio, ffmpeg) · at-rest encryption · local CLI or web interface
phases.desc: records and transcribes audio on the device; audio and transcript stay local, encrypted at rest.

phases.title: ipfs gateway
phases.hardware: Raspberry Pi 5 or RISC-V SBC · NVMe SSD · gigabit ethernet · optional NPU for on-device detection (Coral/Hailo)
phases.software: Kubo or iroh · local HTTP gateway · client-side encryption for private content · on-device face/PII detection at upload · contestation registry with auto-unpin · on-chain node reputation
phases.desc: a self-run ipfs node and gateway: knowledge publishes as CC0, personal content stays encrypted, and anyone identifiable in a file can contest it off the network — anytime, the right never expires.

phases.title: local agents
phases.hardware: one or more Raspberry Pi / mini-PC / NPU boards · ATECC608 for credentials · local network
phases.software: small local models (llama.cpp / Ollama) · agent orchestrator · inter-agent messaging · secret handling on the secure element · in-transit and at-rest encryption
phases.desc: small models run agent tasks on the device; credentials sit on the secure element; messages between agents stay encrypted.

phases.title: surveillance scanner
phases.hardware: Adafruit Feather or Raspberry Pi · broadband RF detector or SDR (RTL-SDR/HackRF) · IR LEDs and sensor for lens glint · magnetometer · OLED / LEDs / haptic · LiPo battery
phases.software: MCU firmware (RF sweep, sensor reads) · detection thresholds · spectrum FFT · alert interface
phases.desc: scans a room for hidden cameras and microphones via RF, lens reflection, and magnetic field; runs offline.

phases.title: open social
phases.hardware: self-run confidential node — AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX host · local storage · network
phases.software: open feed API · open ranking algorithm · in-enclave runtime · on-chain node attestation · client SDK
phases.desc: a fully open social protocol: the API and ranking algorithm are open and run on confidential nodes anyone can run locally; node integrity is attested on a dedicated chain.

phases.title: video transcoder
phases.hardware: AMD EPYC 7003 'Milan' · SP3 board · ECC RDIMM · SEV-SNP · NVIDIA GPU
phases.software: FFmpeg with H.264/H.265/AV1 · SEV-SNP firmware and measurement tooling · job-distribution layer · media encryption
phases.desc: transcodes video inside a confidential VM whose memory the host cannot read; work distributes across nodes.
